The deceased was identified as Al-Amin, 35, of Baripota village under Nabharan union.

The incident took place around 10:30pm in Baripota village.

According to police and local residents, Al-Amin was on his way home after Taraweeh prayers when a group of miscreants attacked him. The attackers stabbed him with sharp weapons indiscriminately, leaving him critically injured, and fled the scene.

Locals rescued him in a bloodied condition and rushed him to Sharsha Upazila Health Complex, where the on-duty doctor declared him dead.

Confirming the incident, Officer-in-Charge (OC) of Sharsha Police Station, Maruf Hasan said he is currently on leave, and the inspector (investigation) is looking into the matter.

Inspector (Investigation) Shah Alam of the same police station said police have already started working to identify the motive behind the murder and those involved.

Photo: Collected Police have arrested a youth in connection with an attempt to attack Abdullah Al Amin, a candidate of the National Citizen Party (NCP) for the Narayanganj-4 constituency.

The youth was arrested around 3:00am today after he initially fled from the scene, confirmed Anowar Hossain, inspector (investigation) of Fatullah Model Police Station.

The arrestee has been identified as Al Amin alias "Akka-Bakka Alamin", 24, of Gaibandha Sadar. He had been living in a rented house in Bashmuli area of Poshchim Deobhog under Kashipur union, from where he was arrested.

Meanwhile, in a press release, Rab-11 said, they have arrested the prime suspect, Maruf Hasan, in connection with the attempted attack on the NCP leader during a special drive in the Char Kashipur area around 2:00am. According to Rab-11 Deputy Director Abdur Rashid, investigation showed that Maruf was accompanying Al Amin during the incident; when suspicion was raised towards Al Amin, he fled the scene.

Maruf, 22, is the son of late Ayub Ali of Char Kashipur, the statement said.

Rab-11 Deputy Director Abdur Rashid also said the suspect has been handed over to Fatullah Police Station.

The incident took place around 7:30pm yesterday, during a door-to-door campaign on referendum. At least two NCP activists were injured during a scuffle, said candidate Abdullah Al Amin, who is also the party’s joint member secretary.

Speaking to The Daily Star over the phone, Abdullah said he was campaigning with around 40 to 50 party activists, interacting with local residents while walking through the area.

“At one point, we noticed a young man following us. On suspicion, we stopped and searched him and found a machete hidden inside his clothes,” he said.

Asked why he was carrying the weapon, the youth claimed that someone has instructed him to follow them with it, Abdullah added.

Describing the area as a hub for drug dealers and juvenile gang members, he said more people quickly gathered at the spot, and taking advantage of the situation, the armed man managed to flee.

“Local residents then advised me to leave the area immediately, and I was safely taken away in a vehicle,” he said.

A general diary has been filed with the Fatullah Police Station today, where Abdullah mentioned previously receiving threats over phone.
summary: General diary filed with the Fatullah Police Station

Photo: Collected A nine-year-old girl from Cox’s Bazar, who was struck by a stray bullet fired from Myanmar on Sunday, has been placed on life support at the National Institute of Neurosciences and Hospital (NINS) in Dhaka.

"Her condition is still very critical, and she is under observation at the Intensive Care Unit (ICU)," Humayun Kabir Himu, an associate professor at NINS, and her uncle, Shawkat Ali, told The Daily Star today.

Huzaifa Afnan, a class-3 student from the Teschi Bridge area of Whykong union, was shot during intense clashes between the Arakan Army and Rohingya armed groups inside Myanmar.

She was rushed to Chattogram Medical College Hospital and later shifted to NINS last night after doctors at CMCH failed to remove the bullet lodged in her throat.

Humayun said the bullet remained stuck in her throat, but she suffered a stroke as it damaged the veins that supply blood to the brain.

This also increased pressure on her brain, and she was put on mechanical ventilation (life support), he said, adding that she had been given medication to reduce the pressure.

She is very young and is showing some response -- two positive signs -- but nothing can be said for certain at this stage, Humayun said. The next procedure may be carried out once the pressure on her brain eases, he added.

A board led by NINS Director Prof Kazi Gias Uddin Ahmed is overseeing her treatment. No decision has yet been taken about sending her abroad for better treatment.
summary: Doctor says bullet lodged in throat caused stroke

The incident took place in Mahendranagar area of Sadar upazila while she was walking from Lalmonirhat town towards Kurigram. Following the incident, Detective Branch (DB) of police and Sadar thana police conducted a joint operation and arrested a young man accused in the case.

The victim filed a case at Lalmonirhat Sadar Police Station under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act. Lalmonirhat DB Officer-in-Charge Saad Ahmed confirmed the incident yesterday.

The arrested man has been identified as Abu Kalam, 31, of Kashipur village under Mahendranagar union.

According to police, the female tourist had been travelling on foot across different districts of the country for the past month. After arriving in Lalmonirhat, she visited several tourist spots in the district. Later, she set out on foot for Kurigram on the morning of January 11.

When she reached Mahendranagar area, about six kilometres from Lalmonirhat town, she needed to use a toilet. At that time, she went to a roadside house and sought permission to use the toilet. While returning from the toilet, Abu Kalam, a resident of the house, allegedly harassed her and attempted to outrage her modesty.

When the victim screamed, other members of the household rushed to the spot. However, instead of seeking justice, they allegedly tried to assault her by accusing her of theft. Somehow, the female tourist managed to leave the house and went live on Facebook, tearfully describing the entire incident. The video went viral on social media within moments.

In the Facebook live video, the female tourist said, “I set out to travel the country on foot one month ago. Before coming to Lalmonirhat, I visited many districts. I did not face any problems anywhere. But after coming to Lalmonirhat, I had to face such an unpleasant situation.”

She further said, “It is very painful to think about our social system. I was harassed and sought justice, but instead, an attempt was made to label me a thief.”

Yesterday afternoon, the victim told journalists that after watching her Facebook live video, DB police quickly arranged for her security.

“I do not know the accused man. But the police identified him within a short time and arrested him,” she said.

OC Saad said, “After watching the Facebook live video, we took immediate action. After the incident, the accused fled his house. Later, with the help of the local police, he was arrested.”

He added that the victim is now in a stable condition and has once again set out to travel the country on foot.
summary: Lalmonirhat DB arrests the suspect after victim’s Facebook live video goes viral

According to police, the attackers set fire to the homes of members of the Hindu, Buddhist and hill communities. The same group had also planned to torch educational institutions ahead of the election to draw greater media attention.

Police yesterday arrested six more people in connection with the arson attacks on residential houses. Chattogram Range Deputy Inspector General (DIG) Ahsan Habib Palash disclosed the information at a press conference at the Chattogram District Police office following the arrests.

With the latest arrests, a total of seven people have been detained so far in connection with the incidents. Police said a group of around 16 to 17 members was involved at different stages of the attacks.

Police also seized various materials used in the arson attacks, along with a CNG-run auto-rickshaw and a motorcycle.

The arrestees were identified as Mohammad Omar Faruk, Mohammad Kabir Hossain, Kartik De, Biplab Barua, Mohammad Lokman and Md Parvez. Earlier, police arrested another individual named Monir.

Speaking at the press conference, DIG Palash said, “Many of those who have been arrested are members of a banned organisation. They believed that by creating an embarrassing situation in the country, many of their leaders would get an opportunity to return to the country and a favourable environment would be created for them.”

However, the DIG did not disclose the name of the banned organisation.

“We have identified one individual who is the mastermind and played an active leadership role in the incidents. He is involved in the local nursery business. We have obtained the names of several others and we are trying to arrest them. A former commissioner affiliated with the banned organisation provided financial support to those involved in implementing the plan,” the police official said.

DIG Palash further said, “The arson attacks were carried out to prove that communal harmony does not exist in Bangladesh and that Hindu, Buddhist and hill communities are not safe here, so that Bangladesh would be embarrassed internationally. The intention was to make the upcoming national election questionable -- if these communities are portrayed as unsafe, it would be claimed that a proper election environment does not exist.

“Initially, the incidents did not receive the level of attention the attackers had expected. As a result, the pace of their activities gradually increased, and in the last couple of incidents, entire houses were completely gutted in arson attacks. From interrogation so far, we have learned that they prepared a plot to set fire to educational institutions to attract greater media attention."

“No specific community was targeted under this arson ‘package’ -- Hindus, Muslims and Buddhists were all among the victims. Through these incidents, an attempt was made to create communal tension inside the country and, on the other hand, to spread propaganda about minority persecution in Bangladesh to mislead the international community and put the government in an awkward position,” he added.

Police said investigations are ongoing to identify others involved in the incidents.

In December last year, several arson attacks took place in Raozan and Rangunia late at night after doors were locked from the outside. Police also recovered several handwritten banners from areas adjacent to the crime scenes. However, no casualties were reported.
summary: Police claim attacks aimed to create communal tension and undermine election credibility

Alcohol, yaba and cannabis were seized from the house that belonged to Abdullah Al Jahir, an additional deputy inspector general of police.

Jahir had rented out the house, where drug use and illegal “DJ parties” had allegedly been going on for a long time, prompting police to conduct the raid, Shafiqul Islam, additional commissioner (detective) of Dhaka Metropolitan Police, told The Daily Star.

Parties and drug consumption were regularly reported at the property in Police Housing-1, said Elias Kabir, deputy commissioner of DB’s Uttara division that conducted the raid.

Jahir was the primary organiser of the parties and a man named Mahbub Alam acted as the co-organiser, according to Elias.

Mahbub told investigators that Jahir received 70 percent of the earnings from the parties, while he took the rest, according to DB. The property was available for bookings through Airbnb, and “DJ parties” were regularly organised for those who booked it.

The arrestees have been sent for summary trial, Elias said.

Meanwhile, following the incident, Jahir, an officer from the 24th police batch, has been attached to the Police Headquarters.

Speaking to The Daily Star, Jahir said that his house had facilities for hosting birthday parties and family gatherings.

They take bookings through Airbnb, but drugs and “DJ parties” are prohibited under their rules. Those who violated the restrictions were blacklisted and fined, he said.

Regarding Monday night’s incident, Jahir said the property had been rented out for a birthday party, but the guests brought drugs, which were recovered during the DB raid.

“What is our crime here? We rented out the property. Our guidelines explicitly prohibit drugs and DJ parties. Those found with drugs committed criminal offences,” he said, while dismissing allegations that such parties were organised every day.

Every month, two to three parties were held at the venue, Jahir added.

Meanwhile, Opposition Leader and Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman has expressed concern over the country’s deteriorating law and order situation following the recovery of drugs and arrests.

The involvement of a property belonging to a senior police official in such an incident has created concern and fear among the public, he said in a Facebook post.

The incident itself reflected the extent of the deterioration in law and order across the country.

Extortion, snatching, looting, robbery and other criminal and anti-social activities had reached alarming levels, he said.

Photo: Forest Department Trees are allegedly being felled and uprooted in a reserved forest at Char Signboard in Patuakhali’s Rangabali upazila to make way for watermelon cultivation, with an excavator being used to build an embankment.

The Forest Department has filed two cases and lodged a GD with police over the alleged destruction. However, attempts to occupy the land have reportedly continued, with forest officials alleging obstruction and threats.

The dispute centres on a two-year lease of 30 acres within the reserved forest. The Forest Department has twice asked the district administration to cancel it, saying the land falls within a protected forest area.

According to Forest Department sources, 415 acres at Char Signboard were declared a reserved forest on April 4, 2010. Mangrove species were planted there, including jhau trees on 10 hectares during the 2021-22 fiscal year.

Photo: Forest Department Amir Hossain, ranger of Rangabali Range, said the district administration leased out 30 acres in the area last year. He alleged that leaseholders Arif Mir and Manik Molla cut trees from a jhau plantation to prepare the land for watermelon cultivation.

The two cases are pending in court. Despite this, work to build an embankment using an excavator began on October 17, allegedly under Arif Mir’s leadership, he said.

“After receiving reports that 200-300 chaila, keora and jhau trees had been uprooted, forest officials tried to stop the work, but it continued despite their objections.”

The department lodged a GD with Rangabali Police Station on October 17, naming three people, including Arif Mir, said the ranger, adding that forest officials had faced obstruction before and that staff shortages often forced them to retreat.

Contacted, Arif Mir denied attempting to grab forest land.

“We have taken a government lease of the land,” he said, but declined to show the lease document or disclose how much he had paid.

This correspondent obtained a permission document issued to 25 farmers by the Rangabali upazila land office on October 13, 2025, bearing the signature of the then upazila nirbahi officer (UNO).

The document allowed cultivation for one season or one year and stated that it could not be used as an official government document in court. It did not identify the issuing official or specify the issuance date or revenue collected.

In a letter dated October 15, Divisional Forest Officer Mohammad Zahidur Rahman Mia urged the deputy commissioner to cancel the lease, warning that it could threaten the forest, wildlife, biodiversity and surrounding mangrove ecosystem.

Rangabali UNO Nazmul Hasan said no such permission had been granted since he took office.

“I do not know how the land was leased out. However, an initiative has been taken to identify forest land and khas land in consultation with the forest department and the leaseholders,” he said, adding that action would be taken if anyone had cut trees.

Abdul Qaiyum, additional deputy commissioner (revenue) of Patuakhali, said the administration was examining the forest department’s letter.

“We are verifying the information and will take action in accordance with the rules. We will also investigate whether there were any irregularities in granting permission for cultivation in the past,” he said.

The other three bodies were recovered in Jhenaidah, Kurigram and Rangpur.

Police recovered the decomposed body of an unidentified man, aged around 35-40, from a pond at Shah Makhdum Institute Public Library in Rajshahi city this morning.

The body was recovered around 9:00am following information from local residents, said Md Gaziur Rahman, spokesperson for Rajshahi Metropolitan Police (RMP).

He said the man might have died two to three days ago, possibly by drowning or due to other causes. His identity could not be established immediately as decomposition had disfigured his face and body.

A 35-year-old man was allegedly hacked to death with an axe by his father-in-law while sleeping at his in-laws’ house in Bolibhadrpur village of Maheshpur upazila around 6:30am today.

The deceased was identified as Golam Rahman alias Abdur Rahman.

Locals detained Golam’s father-in-law Tarikul Islam, 45, after he allegedly walked around carrying the axe following the killing, and handed him over to police. The victim’s wife was also taken to the police station for questioning.

According to local sources, Golam married Tarikul’s eldest daughter, Hazera Khatun, two years ago. As Hazera was staying at her parents’ home, Golam visited his in-laws last night. The following morning, Tarikul allegedly attacked him with an axe while he was asleep.

Abdus Sattar, a former union parishad member, said Tarikul had a history of mental health problems and had previously been kept in a psychiatric institution.

Maheshpur Police Station OC Imran Alam said there had been longstanding tensions between the two men over family disputes. Police recovered the body and the axe allegedly used in the killing. The motive remains under investigation.

Police recovered the body of Moksed Ali alias Bachchu Mia, 61, with his throat slit from a bedroom at his nephew’s house in Panditpara area under Dharanibari union in Ulipur upazila early today.

Bachchu Mia, a resident of Rangpur city, had come to visit his village home and was staying at his nephew Mithu Mia’s house. Police received information about the murder through the national emergency service around 2:20am. The victim’s elder sister, Mazeda Begum, identified the body.

Ulipur Police Station OC Shawkat Ali said police had prepared an inquest report and sent the body to Kurigram General Hospital morgue for autopsy. The motive and those responsible remained unknown, and no arrests had been made as of this morning.

The process of filing a case and taking further legal action was underway.

Fakhrul Alam Ratan, 50, a member of the Balapara Union Awami League, was attacked by several assailants wielding sharp weapons on a road in front of his home in Haricharan Laskar village of Kaunia upazila yesterday afternoon.

According to police, quoting relatives and eyewitnesses, the attackers surrounded Ratan and hacked him indiscriminately before fleeing. Local residents rescued him and took him to hospital, where a doctor declared him dead.

Ratan had previously worked for a non-governmental organisation but later left the job to look after his land and property.

File photo Dhaka-6 lawmaker Ishraque Hossain resigned from the council of ministers yesterday after facing growing criticism over his role in an “anti-drug drive” in which he was seen brandishing a firearm.

Ishraque, who on Sunday denied reports that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had earlier instructed him to resign, said he had voluntarily expressed his intention to quit as state minister for Liberation War Affairs.

“The official version would naturally be that I was asked to resign on the prime minister’s instructions, rather than at my own request,” he said at a media briefing at the Jatiya Press Club in the afternoon.

He said he wanted to resign to focus more on an anti-drug campaign and other public activities in Dhaka-6 and surrounding areas, and the prime minister had agreed to let him do that.

Defending his actions, Ishraque, son of former Dhaka City mayor Sadeque Hossain Khoka, said he would apologise if he had done anything wrong but maintained that he had committed no mistake during the drive.

Ishraque’s resignation letter was sent after the media briefing, said his press officer, Mahfuz Kabir Mukta.

The letter reached the cabinet division at 6:00pm yesterday, said one of its top officials, adding that it was forwarded to the Prime Minister’s Office.

A gazette notification related to the resignation could be issued at any time.

The controversy erupted after Ishraque posted a video on his Facebook account on Saturday of himself getting out of a vehicle with a pistol during an anti-drug drive in the capital’s Gendaria area.

Other footage appeared to show people accompanying him carrying firearms. In one video, a person was seen threatening to shoot, while another showed a bodyguard kicking a young man.

The following day, several media outlets reported that the prime minister had instructed him in the afternoon to step down.

Ishraque dubbed the news as false and fabricated, but at around 8:30am yesterday, he called the press conference.

There, he said confusion had arisen over the timing and process of the announcement: an official decision was supposed to be communicated through the prescribed process, but one of his colleagues disclosed the matter ahead of schedule.

Until the prime minister’s instructions were formally announced, the matter should be treated as a rumour or untrue, he said, adding that he received the formal decision on yesterday morning.

“Whether it happened yesterday or today, what difference does it make? It happened.”

Ishraque defended Saturday’s anti-drug operation, saying it had been coordinated with local law enforcement agencies and aimed at dismantling drug distribution networks.

He expressed disappointment that public discussion had focused on the firearm rather than the campaign.

Ghuntighar and Munshitek had become hubs for drug distribution, and the operation targeted drug dens, he said, adding that six people were handed over to police with evidence.

The local officers-in-charge and Dhaka Metropolitan Police (DMP) deputy commissioners overseeing his constituency were aware of and involved in the operation, he said, describing it as part of efforts coordinated through the Dhaka-6 law and order committee.

The DMP, however, ordered an investigation into the incident, assigning the Wari division to look into it.

Ishraque said he had two firearms registered in his name and that one had been carried briefly for his protection.

The Firearms Policy 2025 allows licensed firearms for self-defence but bars their display in ways that may cause fear or annoyance.

He maintained that he had acted properly and wanted to ensure that no one was harmed.

“I believe I did the right thing in the proper way. I went there, risking my life. People may say that, though I do not care. If someone fires from a rooftop, we do not know whose head the bullet will hit.”

Locals had applauded the drive, he said, adding that he would continue working to meet their expectations.

He went on to urge the media and the public to focus on identifying the main suppliers behind drug distribution rather than concentrating only on street-level dealers.

Asked whether he was considering contesting the Dhaka mayoral election, the 39-year-old said the decision rested entirely with his party and its chairman.

He contested the 2020 mayoral election and had since worked on the capital’s problems under the party’s guidance.

“I am 100 percent prepared if the party decides to nominate me for the election,” he said, adding that he would make every effort to ensure the victory of whoever the party nominated.

The death toll was more than two-and-a-half times the 73 deaths recorded in political clashes during the same period.

The incidents of mob violence reportedly stemmed from allegations of theft, robbery, mugging, rape and hurting religious sentiments, as well as attempts to establish dominance.

The report, signed by HRSS Executive Director Ijajul Islam, was compiled using reports from 16 national dailies and the organisation’s investigations between January and September.

According to the report, 1,013 incidents of political violence left 73 dead and 6,473 injured. Of these, 931 incidents, or 91 percent, involved BNP infighting or clashes with rival parties.

BNP infighting alone accounted for 342 incidents, leaving 40 dead and 2,632 injured. Among the 73 people killed in political violence, 46 were from the BNP, eight from Jamaat-e-Islami and six from the Awami League.

At least 17 people died in law enforcement custody or in incidents involving torture, shootings and so-called “gunfights”, while 10 died while fleeing police chases.

Another 95 inmates, including 55 undertrial prisoners, 20 AL men and one BNP activist, died in jail.

Under the Cyber Protection Ordinance 2025 and Cyber Protection Act 2026, 113 people were sued and 55 arrested in 40 cases. Another 12 were detained over objectionable posts about Prime Minister Tarique Rahman and 24 for allegedly hurting religious sentiments.

Fifty-one journalists were sued in 19 cyber cases. Overall, 518 journalists faced attacks or harassment in 288 incidents, leaving 297 injured and 20 arrested.

Police also foiled 58 rallies, leaving 439 people injured and 46 detained.

Along the Indian border, 43 attacks by the BSF killed 13 Bangladeshis and injured 39. Landmines laid by the Arakan Army along the Myanmar border killed eight and injured five.

The report also recorded abuse of 2,404 women and girls. At least 657 were raped, including 392 minors and 130 gang-rape victims, while 29 were murdered after rape.

Domestic violence claimed the lives of 457 women, while 494 children died in 1,810 incidents of abuse.

Meanwhile, 56 attacks on minorities resulted in the vandalism of 21 temples and 47 homes, while 535 workers died in workplace incidents.

Photo: Courtesy The family of Nazrul Islam, one of the two Bangladeshis executed in Saudi Arabia on October 14, yesterday alleged that Saudi authorities had executed him without notifying them beforehand or giving him an opportunity to defend himself.

Nazrul, 22, the eldest of four siblings, left for Saudi Arabia on November 10, 2022, and worked as a cleaner, according to his family.

Six months after his departure, Saudi police arrested him and a Bangladeshi woman for allegedly committing an “immoral act” at a mosque in Makkah.

More than three years later, his family said it learnt from media reports that he had been executed in Makkah on October 14.

His mother said he spoke to the family by phone from prison every Sunday, but they received no advance notice of his execution.

However, it could not yet be independently verified what charges Nazrul faced, whether he received legal assistance, or whether he was given an opportunity to defend himself before his execution.

The Bangladesh government has yet to officially verify the identities of the two people executed.

Nazrul’s father Abdul Basir said, “If my son was executed without just cause, I want justice.”

Rahima Begum, Nazrul’s mother, has repeatedly broken down in tears since learning of her son’s death. The family also said Nazrul’s paternal aunt, Abeda Begum, died of a heart attack after hearing the news on Wednesday night.

The family has urged the government to investigate the circumstances surrounding his execution and arrange for his body to be brought home at state expense. Neighbours have also called for support for the family.

Nazrul’s father, who had borrowed Tk 7 lakh to send his son to Saudi Arabia, also spoke of how the creditors were now pressuring him to repay the debt.

Contacted, Brahmanbaria Deputy Commissioner Md Abu Sayeed said, “We have received no instructions from higher authorities, and the family has not submitted any application either. If the body is brought back to Bangladesh, we will provide assistance in accordance with the rules, as he was a resident of Brahmanbaria.”

Meanwhile, the Bangladesh government has yet to officially confirm that the two people executed in Saudi Arabia were Bangladeshi nationals and has sought an explanation from Riyadh over an apparent lapse in information-sharing.

Speaking to reporters at the foreign ministry yesterday afternoon, State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said media reports had identified the two as Bangladeshis, but the government was still seeking further details.

An official at the Bangladesh mission in Jeddah, speaking on condition of anonymity, told The Daily Star that both were executed on charges of “adultery”.

The official said Saudi authorities had provided only names and offences, making it difficult to verify their identities or establish whether they were the two who had been executed.

Stressing that the two countries maintain strong bilateral ties and are both signatories to the Vienna Convention,, Humaiun said,”So why was there a gap in the exchange of information? We have sought an explanation from Saudi Arabia.

“There is definitely a gap here, a lapse somewhere in the process, and we are trying to determine the extent of the issue. At the same time, it is deeply disappointing that the executions took place over these alleged offences.”

The state minister also said Bangladesh expected Saudi Arabia to share information about detained Bangladeshi nationals, just as Dhaka would if Saudi nationals were detained in Bangladesh.

“If we detain any Saudi national here, we will certainly inform Saudi Arabia so that consular services can be extended to that person. Similarly, we expect the same for Bangladeshis.”

According to the foreign ministry, the two were accused of committing “adultery” inside a mosque in Makkah.

Saudi authorities arrested, tried and executed them without notifying Dhaka in advance. Bangladesh learnt of the executions on October 14 and subsequently sought details from Riyadh.

Opposition Leader and Bangladesh Jamaat-e-Islami Ameer Shafiqur Rahman yesterday questioned the roles of the government and the Bangladesh mission in Saudi Arabia following the execution of two Bangladeshis.

In a Facebook post around 7:30pm, Shafiqur said, “The government and the Bangladesh embassy are bound to make their positions clear on this matter.”

He pointed out that a large number of Bangladeshis work in Saudi Arabia and other Middle Eastern countries, and that Bangladesh maintains diplomatic missions abroad to safeguard the interests of expatriates, as well as the country’s dignity and national interests.

But the 39-year-old Dhaka-6 MP had repeatedly embarrassed his party over the years, even as his popularity among its rank and file grew.

Ultimately, it was his pistol-wielding, drug-busting “operation” that cost him his post as state minister for Liberation War affairs.

Ishraque’s father, Sadeque Hossain Khoka, was an influential BNP leader with a strong following in the constituency. Ishraque became active in politics around the 2018 national election and soon established himself as a formidable organiser on the streets.

In 2020, he ran for mayor of Dhaka South but lost to the Awami League candidate before challenging the result. He was declared victorious in 2025 but was never sworn in. He then contested the 2026 parliamentary election and won the Dhaka-6 seat.

Here is a look back at some of his most talked-about moments.

The hero who snatched a BNP activist from police

On February 13, 2023, a rally was held in front of the National Press Club to protest a move to revoke the gallantry award conferred on BNP founder Ziaur Rahman.

During the rally, police were about to detain a BNP activist injured in a baton charge when Ishraque intervened, jostling with officers and pulling the activist away. He was also injured in the scuffle.

Ishraque later shared a video of the incident on Facebook, which went viral. He declared that neither baton charges nor cannon fire would stop him from protecting a party worker as long as he was alive.

The incident propelled him into the spotlight and earned him immense popularity among BNP activists.

A presser with Biden’s ‘adviser’

On October 28, 2023, following clashes surrounding BNP’s grand rally, a man named Zahidul Islam, alias Mia Arefi, appeared at the party’s Naya Paltan office, claiming to be an adviser to then US president Joe Biden.

He spoke to journalists while seated beside Ishraque and retired lieutenant general Chowdhury Hasan Sarwardy. The next day, police detained Arefi at the airport, and all three were named in a case filed with Paltan Police Station.

Ishraque and Sarwardy were accused of helping Arefi address journalists under a false identity.

The incident caused major embarrassment for the BNP, which issued a statement distancing itself from Arefi’s activities. Ishraque later expressed regret on Facebook.

After the July Uprising toppled the Awami League government and the courts ruled in favour of Ishraque’s claim to the mayoral post, his battle for office took a new turn.

In May 2025, he and his supporters laid siege to city hall after the interim government declined to administer his oath of office. Essential services were disrupted, causing public sufferings.

Ishraque even threatened to swear himself into office. While his loyalists saw the protests as a show of strength, the disruption and mounting public sufferings drew flak.

Eventually, Ishraque backed down without ever assuming office as mayor.

Ishraque went viral again on December 22, 2025, but this time for pushing and shoving his own party men to make his way to the front of a crowd.

He had visited the grave of BNP founder Ziaur Rahman to pay respects with the newly formed Bangladesh Jatiyotabadi Muktijoddha Projonmo.

He later expressed regret on Facebook but, as he would do repeatedly, offered an explanation that only deepened his embarrassment. He said he was being “firm” in “setting the lines right”.

Ishraque made headlines again during the swearing-in of newly elected members of parliament on February 17, 2026. Arriving late, he missed the oath-taking ceremony with his party colleagues and had to join the opposition and independent MPs instead.

Although Ishraque abstained from taking the oath as a member of the Constitution Reform Council, in line with his party’s decision, he appeared unsure what to do next.

Then he spotted independent MP Rumeen Farhana hurriedly gathering her belongings and leaving the hall after taking the parliamentary oath. Ishraque promptly followed her out, seemingly relieved to have found a cue.

Saluting with the service chiefs

Last July, after Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad took over as president, he visited the National Memorial in Savar to pay tribute to the martyrs.

Ishraque, then state minister for Liberation War affairs, was among those present, alongside the chiefs of the three defence services.

When the three chiefs lined up and saluted the martyrs, Ishraque, standing alongside them, raised his hand in salute too. It was another viral moment, sparking a flood of memes.

Ishraque later said his hand rose in salute almost on its “own volition” whenever “freedom fighters” were mentioned, and that he would continue saluting them whenever and wherever he could.

Ishraque’s ministry organised a reception for martyrs’ families and July fighters at Agargaon to mark the second anniversary of the July Uprising.

Leaders of the National Citizen Party alleged that a documentary screened at the event failed to accurately portray the movement, leading to heated exchanges.

Instead of defusing the tension, Ishraque took the podium and began shouting, further angering the protesters. Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed also failed to calm the situation, and the protesters eventually walked out of the venue.

On October 17, 2026, Ishraque jumped out of a car, pistol in hand.

He ran towards men attempting to flee, followed by his team of activists, who manhandled and kicked those they suspected of being drug peddlers. At least one of his associates was also seen brandishing a firearm.

Ishraque pointed his pistol at the suspects, while someone off-camera threatened to shoot.

The close-up video clips suggested that the MP even had his PR team on hand to film his exploits. That such vigilantism could go horribly wrong with the slightest misstep, and that it was entirely beyond his authority, appeared to have escaped the Dhaka-6 MP.

They said constitutional reform should define the powers of state organs and ensure accountability.

The proposals came at a meeting between academics and the special parliamentary committee on constitutional reform at the Jatiya Sangsad yesterday.

Speaking to reporters after the meeting, Home Minister Salahuddin Ahmed, chair of the committee, said he was unsure whether the opposition’s absence would trigger controversy, but there would be opportunities for debate.

Prof Mohammad Tanzimuddin Khan said proposals had been made to recognise the Liberation War and those who contributed to the independence movement before and during the war.

Forty-five academics were invited to the meeting, but only 17 attended.

Several media outlets reported last night that Prime Minister Tarique Rahman had asked Ishraque to resign from the cabinet following public outrage over his display of a firearm during an "anti-drug operation" in the capital's Gendaria on Saturday.

Citing sources close to the government, the reports said Tarique summoned Ishraque after a cabinet meeting at the Secretariat yesterday afternoon and instructed him to step down.

However, no official statement had been issued by the time this report was filed at 2:00am today.

At 10:34pm, state broadcaster Bangladesh Television ran a news ticker reading: “Prime Minister orders Ishraque to resign from the cabinet.”

The ticker was removed shortly afterwards.

At 11:22pm, BTV aired another ticker quoting Ishraque as saying the reports that he had been instructed to resign were "completely false".

Government and Prime Minister's Office officials said discussions had been underway since yesterday afternoon over whether Ishraque should step down.

The controversy has embarrassed the government and raised concerns at the highest levels about ministerial conduct.

Tarique also reportedly reprimanded Ishraque yesterday afternoon for brandishing a firearm, instructing him to apologise publicly and refrain from doing so again.

Asked about the government's position on Ishraque's conduct, Cabinet Secretary Nasimul Ghani told reporters after a cabinet meeting around 7:15pm, "I have no comment on this matter. There was no discussion in this regard."

Pressed on whether the government had taken note of the incident or launched an inquiry, he said, "I will make no further comment on this."

In a Facebook post around 12:35am today, Ishraque said any instruction from the prime minister to a cabinet member, whether to resign or on any other matter, "is conventionally binding and becomes effective immediately upon issuance".

He added, "Therefore, there is no need to verify such information through any third, fourth, or more distant intermediary.

"If any such decision is taken concerning the Liberation War Affairs ministry or myself, the nation will be informed in detail through a press conference at the earliest possible opportunity once the decision takes effect, Insha'Allah."

Earlier, contacted by The Daily Star around 11:00pm, Ishraque dismissed reports that he had been asked to resign, calling them "rumours".

At 10:30pm, his press officer Mahfuz Kabir issued a statement dismissing reports in the media and on social media that Ishraque had resigned or been asked to resign as "completely false, baseless, fabricated, and motivated".

"The truth is that the state minister continues to discharge his official and political responsibilities with dedication and distinction. No directive has been issued from the highest levels of the government asking him to resign, and there is no question of his resignation.

"At the same time, we call upon those who have published or broadcast these misleading reports to immediately withdraw them and present the correct facts. Otherwise, appropriate legal action will be taken against those responsible for spreading false information."

Three government sources familiar with the matter said Tarique expressed strong dissatisfaction when he met Ishraque at the Secretariat around 2:00pm yesterday, questioning why the state minister had personally participated in the operation while carrying a firearm.

A government official, speaking on condition of anonymity, said, "His actions have embarrassed the government… If the government does not take strong action over the incident, it will create a negative impression among the people. That's why he has been asked to apologise publicly."

Ishraque's actions have also caused unease among BNP ministers, lawmakers and rank-and-file party members.

Five MPs and two ministers, requesting anonymity, said they supported anti-drug drives but objected to a state minister personally carrying out such an operation while armed. They said the incident had exposed the government to criticism.

Some lawmakers also feared the videos could damage the government's image among foreign diplomats.

The controversy erupted on Saturday when videos posted on Ishraque's verified Facebook page showed him stepping out of a vehicle with a pistol and directing his associates to apprehend several people near the Dayaganj Ghuntighar railway crossing, close to Gandaria Railway Station.

Two others accompanying the state minister were also seen carrying firearms. At one point, a member of his entourage threatened to shoot, while one of his bodyguards kicked a young man as the group attempted to detain several people.

The footage went viral, raising questions about the legality of a state minister personally conducting such an operation and displaying a firearm in public.

Under the home ministry's Firearms Licence Issuance, Renewal and Use Policy 2025, licence holders may carry or use firearms for self-defence but are prohibited from displaying them in a manner that causes fear or annoyance to others.

Meanwhile, Ishraque accused several media outlets in a Facebook post of exaggerating the incident.

He said the operation, carried out with assistance from Gandaria police, dismantled four to five makeshift drug dens and led to the detention of six suspected drug traders.

Suspected heroin, foreign liquor, drug paraphernalia, sharp weapons, cash and mobile phones were also seized, he added.

Dhaka Metropolitan Police has also launched an investigation into the incident.

Detective Branch Chief Shafiqul Islam told reporters around noon yesterday that the deputy commissioner of Wari Division had been assigned to investigate and submit a report.

Opposition Jamaat-e-Islami condemned the incident, describing the display of a firearm as an attempt to establish a "reign of terror".

In a statement yesterday, the party said Ishraque's conduct was unlawful, could embolden criminals and amounted to a breach of his oath of office. It called for action against those responsible.

Under Article 58 of the constitution, a minister other than the prime minister vacates office upon submitting a resignation to the prime minister for forwarding to the president.

The prime minister may also request a minister to resign at any time. If the minister fails to comply, the prime minister may advise the president to terminate the appointment.

Responding to Prime Minister Tarique Rahman’s remark that the opposition had failed to uphold the spirit of July, Porwar said Jamaat was committed to that spirit, while the BNP government was acting against it by refusing to implement the referendum verdict and the July Charter.

Tarique Rahman yesterday questioned the opposition leader’s absence from the inauguration of the newly built July Memorial at Osmani Udyan in Dhaka. Porwar was speaking at a press conference at Jamaat’s central office in Moghbazar today, attended by several Jamaat MPs and central leaders.

Explaining Shafiqur’s absence, Porwar said both the Jamaat ameer and its secretary general had received invitations, but the opposition leader had not been accorded the protocol befitting his position.

“As opposition leader, he holds the rank of a minister. He was entitled to that respect at the event. You failed to accord our opposition leader the respect he deserved at the programme,” he said.

“Do you want the leader of such a large opposition party to face humiliation by attending a major government event under such circumstances?” he asked.

“We are upholding the spirit of July. We are taking to the streets to demand implementation of the referendum verdict and the July Charter,” he said.

He accused the BNP government of evading implementation of the referendum verdict and acting against the spirit of the July Charter through partisan appointments to constitutional positions and government institutions.

Citing Jamaat’s assistance to families of those killed during the July Uprising and support for the treatment of the injured, Porwar said the party had also published compilations on the lives and contributions of the martyrs in Bangla, English and Arabic. Porwar said consensus had been reached on 84 issues at the National Consensus Commission. He alleged that the BNP was avoiding implementation of the July Charter by maintaining differences on several fundamental issues.

File Photo: Reuters/ Eva Plevier The World Court yesterday rejected Myanmar's objections to a genocide case over its treatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority, paving the way for the case to be heard in full.

Myanmar, now ruled by a military junta that seized power in 2021, had argued that Gambia, which brought the suit, had no standing to do so at the top UN court, formally known as the International Court of Justice (ICJ).

But presiding Judge Joan Donoghue said the 13 judge panel found that all members of the 1948 Genocide Convention can and are obliged to act to prevent genocide, and the court has jurisdiction in the case.

"Gambia, as a state party to the Genocide convention, has standing," she said, reading a summary of the ruling. The court will now proceed to hearing the merits of the case, a process that will take years.

Bangladesh has welcomed the judgment.

"Bangladesh maintains that the question of international justice and accountability will be critical in finding a durable solution to the Rohingya crisis, and would also prove to be a confidence building measure for the sustainable repatriation of the Rohingyas to their homes in Myanmar with their legitimate rights restored," the Ministry of Foreign Affairs in Dhaka said in a statement.

Gambia, which took up the cause after its then-attorney general visited a refugee camp in Bangladesh, argues that all countries have a duty to uphold the 1948 Genocide Convention. It is backed by the 57-nation Organisation for Islamic Cooperation in a suit aiming to hold Myanmar accountable and prevent further bloodshed.

A separate UN fact-finding mission concluded that a 2017 military campaign by Myanmar that drove 730,000 Rohingyas into neighbouring Bangladesh had included "genocidal acts".

While the court's decisions are binding and countries generally follow them, it has no way of enforcing them.

In a 2020 provisional decision it ordered Myanmar to protect the Rohingya from genocide, a legal victory that established their right under international law as a protected minority.

However, Rohingya groups and rights activists say there has been no meaningful attempt to end their systemic persecution and what Amnesty International has called a system of apartheid.

Rohingyas are still denied citizenship and freedom of movement in Myanmar. Tens of thousands have now been confined to squalid displacement camps for a decade, reports Reuters.

The junta has imprisoned democratic leader Aung San Suu Kyi, who defended Myanmar personally in 2019 hearings in The Hague.
summary: The World Court yesterday rejected Myanmar’s objections to a genocide case over its treatment of the Muslim Rohingya minority, paving the way for the case to be heard in full.

"In many places, load shedding continued for more than an hour. We've seen that a feeder takes 2-3 hours to resume electricity supply after being shut. In many areas, it takes 4 hours. This has happened in my area also. We need one week's time to assess the situation and address it," the state minister told reporters at his Gulshan residence in the capital.

The government will plan its next steps for electricity rationing after analysing the data of the first week of power outages, he said.

The government on Tuesday imposed countrywide power cuts with timetables for specific areas as part of austerity measures to save fuel amid soaring energy prices in the global market.

It also has temporarily shut down all diesel-fired power plants, which contribute 1,000-1,500MW to the national grid daily.

The state minister said new schedules for load shedding will be fixed next week and the situation is likely to improve as time progresses.

He said they would fix another load shedding schedule after having the first week's results.

"Customers are accepting the situation due to special circumstances. I think we can put things in order in 10 days and the situation will get better after that," Nasrul said.

Responding to a question, the state minister said he was expecting that alternative energy (energy sources other than fossil fuels) would be used in some power plants and that is why he was terming the current situation temporary.

He said the demand for power would fall gradually in the "coming season" and they would be able to deal with the situation.

Nasrul, however, said the oil and gas crises would worsen if the Russia-Ukraine war continued, adding that there would not be any problem if people used electricity sensibly.

He also highlighted the differences between the demands for electricity in cities and rural areas. "It is found that three villages collectively use 10MW power every day, but one locality in Dhaka alone uses about 100MW. This is a problem."

He said the demand for gas in factories and industrial units is also increasing. "The majority of our gas supplies are being sent to industries."

The state minister said only 10 percent of the country's total diesel stock is used for power generation and the rest is used by agriculture and transportation sectors.

Nasrul said the overall power supply deficit is now crossing the 1,500MW mark daily. "In the last two-three days, we observed that the load shedding was 1,500 MW every day. Sometimes the figure went up by 400-500MW when the usage of gas increased in industries."

He also said Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation has recently held meetings with the transport sector stakeholders.

"The meetings were held to analyse how much increase in transport fares would be needed if the fuel prices are hiked by the BPC," he said.

The BPC was yet to adjust fuel prices with the additional import prices, the state minister said.
summary: Admitting that the Power Division could not impose schedule-wise power cuts across the country, State Minister for Power, Energy and Mineral Resources Nasrul Hamid yesterday sought one week’s time to address the issue.

The 39-year-old reached the top of the 8,611-metre (28,251-foot) mountain early Thursday, AFP reported yesterday.

According to a 2019 National Geographic article, K2 is widely considered the toughest and most dangerous mountain to climb.

Nicknaming K2 the "Savage Mountain", the article said, "Unlike Everest, it is not possible to 'walk' to the top; all sides of K2 are extremely steep and see frequent rockfalls and avalanches."

Wasfia also climbed Everest, the world's highest peak, in 2012.

On her Facebook page, the mountaineer on Sunday sought thoughts and prayers from her fans and well-wishers saying she was heading out to summit K2 that night with the strongest team.

"If all goes well, good news will come in a week," she wrote.

Wasfia is best known for being the only Bangladeshi to climb the Seven Summits -- the highest mountains of every continent.

Her expedition consisted of some of the strongest and most renowned climbers in the world -- Mingma Tenzi Sherpa, Mingma David Sherpa, and Nirmal Purja.

K2 is deemed notorious for its harsh conditions -- winds can blow at more than 200 kilometres per hour and temperatures can drop to negative 60 degrees Celsius. It has only been scaled by 425 people since 1954 -- including around 20 women.

According to the 2019 National Geographic article, "Of the 14 mountains that rise at least 8,000 metres (26,246 feet), K2 remains the only peak unclimbed during winter."

Located in the Karakorum Range in northern Pakistan near the country's border with China, K2 is thought to be the world's most dangerous mountain.

Pakistan is home to five of the world's 14 mountains higher than 8,000 metres, and climbing them all is considered the ultimate achievement of any mountaineer.
summary: Renowned Bangladeshi mountaineer Wasfia Nazreen conquered the treacherous K2 in Pakistan, becoming the first person from Bangladesh to summit the second-tallest mountain in the world.

title: CU sexual assault: Fingers pointed at BCL men
body:

An officer of Hathazari Police Station, preferring anonymity, told The Daily Star, "From witnesses and substantial evidence, we have gathered that the accused are Chhatra League activists. But their faces could not be identified from the CCTV footage."

According to the CU Proctor Office, the university has around 135 CCTV cameras. However, only half of those have night vision.

Ruhul Amin, officer-in-charge of Hathazari Model Police Station, said, "We are working to arrest those involved in the incident. However, their identities could not be confirmed, as CCTV footage is not clear and of poor quality. But my teams are working and we are hoping to get results soon."

He, however, declined to comment on the involvement of BCL men until the investigation is complete.

Meanwhile, teachers and students of the university alleged the CU administration has been negligent in involving the law enforcers.

Following the incident, former leaders of CU BCL, on their Facebook profiles, criticised the roles of the current Chhatra League leaders and demanded exemplary punishment to the abusers.

The victim, who is a first-year student of the Arts Faculty, filed a case against unidentified people under the Women and Children Repression Prevention Act with Hathazari Police Station on Wednesday night.

In the case statement, she said that on Sunday night a group of five men forcibly picked her and her friend up from Hotashar Mor to the Botanical Garden.

They first beat the two up and then tied up the plaintiff and sexually assaulted her. When her friend tried to save her, the abusers snatched one of their mobile phones and left the area.

Before filing a case with the police, the victim filed a complaint with the proctorial body.

The CU admin, instead of taking measures to punish the perpetrators, instructed the female students to return to their dormitories by 10:00pm "to avoid such situations".

The proctorial body did not inform the police about the sexual assault, a criminal offence, even after receiving a complaint, CU students said.

Proctor Robiul Hasan Bhuiyan, however, refuted the allegation, saying they had informed the police but the victim was unwilling to cooperate initially.

"The [victim] student came to us on Monday morning [a day after the incident]. We immediately started checking the CCTV footage, but she did not recall the exact time. We then asked her to go to the police, but she said she would think about it.

"When she agreed, me and two assistant proctors took her took her to the police station."

There was no negligence on the university authority's end, he added.

Protests against the incident began on Wednesday night, as hundreds of female resident students laid siege to the vice chancellor's office.

They also placed a four-point demand, which included assurance of justice and punishment to the attackers within four working days, and round-the-clock security for all students.

The protesters further demanded the proctorial body step down if it failed to bring justice within four days. 

The female students also asked the administration to properly investigate all the complaints filed with the CU Sexual Harassment Prevention Cell.

Yesterday morning, hundreds of students from CU's chemistry department staged a demonstration in front of the university's administrative building from around 11:00am.

Several teachers from different departments joined them.

Under the banner of Progotishil Chhatra Jote and General Students of CU, the students also brought out a procession from the administrative building and marched towards the Central Shahid Minar.

Addressing the demonstrators, Vice Chancellor Shireen Akhter said the demands would be met as soon as possible.

Meanwhile, BCL central unit has served a show-cause notice to Rezaul Haque Rubel, president of CU BCL, a day after the incident, for violating the organisation's discipline.

BCL insiders said Rubel was served the notice as he had asked the victim not to file a complaint with the CU authorities.

Speaking to The Daily Star, Rubel, however, said he was asked to show cause as he failed to discharge some of his organisational duties. "But my rivals are now trying to link me to this incident."

He claimed he did not ask anyone not to file a complaint; instead, he directly informed the matter to an assistant proctor and an on-duty police official.

Iqbal Hossain Tipu, general secretary of CU BCL, told The Daily Star, "We demand exemplary punishment to the abusers. Their only identity is that they are abusers."

Former CU BCL president Md Alamgir Tipu said, "Those who are directly involved should be punished both academically and legally. If any leader tried to cover up the incident, they should also be withdrawn from their post."

Fazle Rabbi Sugan, former general secretary of CU BCL, told The Daily Star, "As a former BCL leader, I am ashamed. BCL is a renowned organisation and always stands for student rights."

The information about the victim's whereabouts is now being protected. CU Proctor Robiul Islam said, "She is in a safe place under our supervision. We are providing everything she needs. However, for the sake of investigation, her location cannot be disclosed."
summary: Those who sexually assaulted a female student on Chittagong University campus on July 17 night are members of Bangladesh Chhatra League, said police sources and CU BCL insiders.

Unless these projects are of utmost importance, they should be put on hold, he said.

"Bangladesh needs to be wary of the debt situation as well, since it may become somewhat tricky in 2024-26 as the repayment schedule for many of the high value loans will kick off around that time," he said at a virtual dialogue titled Top 20 Mega Projects in Bangladesh: Trends and Status.

"There is a need for defining a repayment strategy, including rescheduling of imminent payments, given the current account and foreign reserve status.

"Very close monitoring will be paramount to keep the debt situation in check."

Debapriya also said the government should review several projects in which there was "visible corruption".

The comments come at a time when the country is struggling with dwindling foreign currency reserves, runaway inflation, and energy crisis.

Debapriya and his team researched on 20 most expensive mega projects, including the Padma Bridge, Padma Bridge Rail Link, Rooppur Nuclear Power Plant, and three metro rail projects.

The total implementation cost of the 20 projects is Tk 556,955.74 crore, of which 61.17 percent is supposed to be foreign assistance.

Foreign sources are supposed to finance over 50 percent of 14 of the 20 projects.

There are 11 transportation and communication sector projects and four electricity and fuel sector projects.

The projects related to electricity and fuel are much larger and more foreign-finance dependent, he said.

There are two education sector projects, two health sector projects, and one housing project, he said.

"It seems that the mega projects have come at the expense of fiscal allocations for social sectors including health, education and social protection."

The lack of transparency and accountability along with delay in implementation have affected the reserve.

Implementation of the 20 mega projects involve 40 loan packages and five grants.

Of the total foreign finance, almost 84.4 percent is in grants and concessional loans. Two semi-concessional loans (4.4 percent) are supposed to come from Russia while five non-concessional loans (11.1 percent) are supposed to come from China.

Thirteen loan packages amounting to $32.26 billion are due for repayment by 2024.

Around 57.5 percent of the loans have a grace period of 10 years while 72.5 percent have repayment period of 20 years and beyond.

Debapriya said the review of terms and conditions of foreign loans for the top 20 mega projects are favourable as there are a good number of concessional loans along with grants.

The economist commented that he saw the negotiation between the government and International Monetary Fund (IMF) as a positive development because an IMF loan will help stabilise the economic condition and improve confidence of foreign investors and development partners.
summary: Given the current economic situation, the government should consider suspending mega projects the physical work of which has yet to begin, economist Debapriya Bhattacharya said yesterday.

"If any train carries passengers on its roof, appropriate actions will be taken against the officials concerned," said the court.

The bench of Justice Md Nazrul Islam Talukder and Justice Khizir Hayat made the remarks during a suo moto proceedings on this issue.

The HC bench ordered the rail authorities to inform it by July 31 what steps have been taken to stop passengers journeying on the train roofs and ticket scalping -- a practice of illegally purchasing tickets for reselling them at an inflated price.

During the proceedings, the HC asked two railway officials, "Why is there so much mismanagement in rail services? Why will ticket scalping take place? Why will people travel on the roof of the trains?"

Such a situation cannot be allowed to continue, the bench observed.

Earlier on the day, Joint Director General of Bangladesh Railway AM Salahuddin and Director (Traffic) Md Nahid Hasan Khan and sohoz.com official Zunayer Hossain appeared before the HC bench to convey the steps taken to prevent mismanagement in the railway services.

AM Salahuddin told the HC bench they have some limitations in preventing passengers from travelling on the roof.

The HC bench then asked the official whether the passengers on the roofs pay fares.

If the passengers are allowed to travel on the roof even after they pay fares, it is outright corruption and must be stopped at any cost, the HC bench said, adding that accidents might take place if people are allowed to be on the roofs.

"You cannot remain silent. This cannot be allowed. You must discharge your duties properly," Justice Nazrul Islam Talukder told the officials.

Deputy Attorney General AKM Amin Uddin Manik told the court the railway authorities have taken steps to form a committee to probe the mismanagement in services.

The issues came to the fore after Dhaka University student Mohiuddin Roni waged a protest lately.

On Wednesday, the HC bench wanted to know about the sit-in programme enforced by Roni demanding improvement of railway services and about the steps taken to this effect.

The bench delivered the order on a suo moto move following a photo of Roni and a caption published on The Daily Star yesterday.

Senior lawyer Khusrhid Alam Khan appeared for the Anti-Corruption Commission during the proceedings.
summary: The High Court yesterday came down hard on Bangladesh Railway for mismanagement, ticket scalping and carrying passengers on the train roofs.

This was announced in a statement issued by Noab yesterday. It means newspapers which now sell for Tk 10 a copy will be sold for Tk 12 and those priced at Tk 5 will be sold for Tk 7.

"The cost of our publication has increased hugely. The price of newsprint, our primary raw material, went up in the middle of last year. The price has doubled in the last few months than in the first half of last year. In addition, the exchange rate of US dollar also increased. Printing costs have also soared because of the rise in prices of ink, plates and other necessary materials."

As transportation costs have also risen, the expenses of newspapers have doubled as a cumulative effect, it added.

On the other hand, Noab over the last few months has repeatedly sought government assistance, but has not received the expected response, said the statement.

"Even though all industries were given stimulus packages by the government, the newspaper industry did not receive any assistance. At the same time, corporate tax, import duty and other taxes [including VAT] remained unchanged in this fiscal year's national budget."

The Noab said the industry is going through an unprecedented crisis.

"We know that our readers and well-wishers are our biggest strength. We are pledge-bound to deliver the best possible newspapers to you. We seek cooperation from all our readers and well-wishers," said Noab.

title: Electricity crisis may worsen
body:
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function() { // Share dropdown toggle const shareToggle = document.querySelector('.share-toggle'); const shareMenu = document.querySelector('.share-menu'); if (shareToggle && shareMenu) { shareToggle.addEventListener('click', function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); shareMenu.classList.toggle('hidden'); }); // Close dropdown when clicking outside document.addEventListener('click', function() { shareMenu.classList.add('hidden'); }); shareMenu.addEventListener('click', function(e) { e.stopPropagation(); }); } // Copy link functionality const copyBtn = document.querySelector('.copy-link-btn'); if (copyBtn) { copyBtn.addEventListener('click', function() { const url = this.getAttribute('data-url'); navigator.clipboard.writeText(url).then(function() { // Show success message const originalText = copyBtn.innerHTML; copyBtn.innerHTML = 'Copied!'; setTimeout(function() { copyBtn.innerHTML = originalText; }, 2000); }); }); } }); Partha Pratim Bhattacharjee Asifur Rahman Partha Pratim Bhattacharjee and Asifur Rahman

The government's plan for one to two hours of daily power cuts is failing, especially in the north, and the signs are that the electricity crisis may worsen across the country in the coming days.

The north is already seeing three to four hours of load shedding a day with Rangpur being the worst affected.

The government on Sunday announced a schedule for area-based power cuts to mitigate the electricity crisis.

Experts have warned that with the dwindling fuel stocks, the duration of power outages would surely increase in the days ahead. They also pointed fingers at underutilised coal-fired plants and inadequate transmission lines.

With the crisis deepening, the government yesterday came up with some new measures to cut power usage. It directed the public offices to cut consumption by 25 percent. Officials have been asked to avoid, as much as possible, having in-person meetings to reduce fuel and electricity consumption.

Bangladesh Power Development Board has been generating 500MW a day more from coal-based plants compared to what it produced on June 29, when the load shedding began.

But the Barapukuria Power Station in Dinajpur has been gobbling up its stocks of coal without replenishment. The coal production at its mine was suspended in late April for underground development work, and the plant would not get fresh coal until the middle of August, said sources.

The plant now has a coal stock for only 15 days, even though it is generating only 200MW with a capacity of 525MW.

An official of the Barapukuria coal mine said the plant might have to stop generation due to the shortage of coal.

Data from Nesco, the power distributor for northern districts, shows it received 500MW yesterday, about half of what it needs.

The demand-supply gap resulted in serious power cuts in the north.

Officials of Dhaka's two distributors -- DPDC and DESCO -- told The Daily Star that they got less power than required and that they could not maintain one to two hours of load shedding in some areas.

Shamim Hasan, director (public relations) of Bangladesh Power Development Board (BPDB), said they received some allegations that the distribution companies failed to maintain the schedule but "that was not at a large scale".

The coal-fired 1,320MW Payra Power Plant is producing 1,000-1,050MW, but it can only supply the power to the Barishal-Khulna region as the transmission line to Dhaka is yet to be completed.

On top of the issues with coal-fired plants, the stock of furnace oil is running low.

A Bangladesh Petroleum Corporation official told The Daily Star, "We have only 1.2 lakh tonnes of furnace oil in stock against the monthly requirement of 55,000 tonnes."

The official said the stock was below the standard practice and the BPC was yet to buy its next consignment of furnace oil.

Bangladesh has a capacity to generate 22,348MW electricity. Of that, around 52 percent is from gas-based plants, 27 percent from furnace oil-based plants, 5.86 percent from diesel-based, 8.03 percent from coal-powered plants, 1 percent from hydro, 0.5 percent from other renewable energies, and 5.27 percent is imported, according to the BPDB data.

The government this week decided to shut 10 diesel power plants. Last month, it stopped importing LNG from the high-priced spot market, and the power cuts began after this.

LNG injection into the national gas grid has slipped further in recent days, Petrobangla data shows.

Yesterday, it was 430 million cubic feet (mmcfd). On June 29, the injection was 854 mmcfd and in the first week of July, it was 500 mmcfd.

The country is generating 12,000-13,000MW electricity a day against a demand of 14,000-14,500MW.

Talking to The Daily Star, energy expert M Shamsul Alam said, "The schedule [for power cuts] was not made to be maintained automatically. It will be manually implemented and the negligence and ignorance of officials may ruin this process."

He observed that there needs to be more professional efficiency.

Amid this situation, the state-owned Chittagong Urea Fertiliser Ltd suspended production due to gas shortage on Tuesday night. Jamuna Fertiliser Company Ltd, the country's largest urea producer, had shut down earlier for the same reason.

Agriculture Minister Muhammad Abdur Razzaque yesterday said the government was trying to find alternative sources of fertiliser. "We're trying to make both Jamuna Fertiliser Company Ltd and Chittagong Urea Fertiliser Ltd operational. The government has to provide gas to bring these two factories back into operation."

Senior secretaries and secretaries of all the ministries and divisions sat at the PMO yesterday to find ways to reduce expenditure.

The meeting, chaired by Prime Minister's Principal Secretary Ahmad Kaikaus, came up with six decisions and recommendations.

It decided that the Finance Division would issue a circular to cut 20 percent energy sector expenditure.

Officials would avoid in-person meetings and foreign trips as much as possible. Markets would be monitored to keep prices of essentials at a tolerable level and action would be taken against hoarders.

The National Board of Revenue will take steps at the beginning of the financial year to increase internal resource mobilisation and to achieve the revenue collection target.

The meeting also asked all ministries to review their procurement plans and take initiatives to reduce expenditure.

Talking to reporters afterwards, Kaikaus said, "There's no reason to panic. These are precautionary measures so that we don't have to face any kind of crisis in the future."

He urged non-government organisations to follow suit.

Hours after the meeting, the water resources ministry issued an office order asking its officials to avoid personal use of government vehicles and set the thermostats at 26 degrees Celsius at the Pani Bhaban.
summary: The government’s plan for one to two hours of daily power cuts is failing, especially in the north, and the signs are that the electricity crisis may worsen across the country in the coming days.

BNP leaders said they shunned the talks because it was impossible for the EC to hold a free and fair election under the incumbent government.

Election commissioners yesterday said  they would "wait" for the BNP until the election and they might contact the opposition parties "time and again".

Late last month, the BNP and several other parties skipped the EC's views-exchange programmes on electronic voting machines.

BNP Standing Committee Member Khandakar Mosharraf Hossain said, "Our decision is that we will not join an election under the current government. We have not joined the process of forming this Election Commission, have not given them recognition, and have not taken part in any activities of the commission. We have not changed our stance and that is why we did not join the talks."

While talking to reporters at the EC office, Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Kazi Habibul Awal said he would not comment on whether the commission will take any special measures to bring the BNP to the dialogue.

Election Commissioner Md Alamgir said, "It would have been better if they [the BNP] joined the talks. The talks are going well because political parties are giving thoughtful opinions. These will help us hold a better election.

"We are repeatedly taking initiatives to [bring the BNP to the talks]. We will contact them time and again."

The EC's latest talks with political parties started on Sunday. Eleven parties have participated while the BNP, Bangladesh Kalyan Party and Bangladesh Muslim League shunned the talks.

On March 13, the EC began another round of talks with a cross section of people, including educationists, civil society members, journalists, former CECs and ECs, and local election observers.

The CEC yesterday said, "It is really our sole responsibility to ensure that every voter can cast their vote freely. This is the foundation of democracy. And for this, everyone's cooperation is needed. Every party has said they believe in political consensus. Whether there is consensus or not, we said we will continue our efforts."
summary: The BNP yesterday skipped Election Commission’s dialogue seeking recommendations of political parties on how to hold a free and fair general election.
